title: Finland – Forestry services – Metsänhoidon palvelusopimus 2027-2028 (2029-2030)
description: Mäntsälän kunta pyytää tarjoustanne metsänhoidon palvelusopimuksesta, jonka tavoitteena on turvata talous- ja puistometsien laadukas metsänhoito, hakkuumahdollisuuksien täysimääräinen ja suunnitelmallinen hyödyntäminen talousmetsissä, maisemanhoito ja virkistysmahdollisuuksien huomioiminen sekä tilaajan edunvalvonta metsänhoitoon liittyvissä asioissa. Metsäpalvelusopimus laaditaan vuosille 2027-2028 ja sopimusta voidaan jatkaa yhdellä kahden (2) vuoden mittaisella optiokaudella. Mäntsälän kunta omistaa noin 870 hehtaaria metsää, jota hoidetaan vuosille 2024–2033 laaditun metsäsuunnitelman mukaisesti. Metsäsuunnitelma on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Suunnitelman keskeinen periaate on, että hakkuut ja metsänhoitotyöt kilpailutetaan erikseen, jotta kunta saa puukaupasta parhaan tuoton ja töistä kustannustehokkaan toteutuksen. Palveluntuottaja suunnittelee, kilpailuttaa ja valvoo metsänhoitotyöt kunnan lukuun. Työt tilataan kunnan vuosisuunnitelman mukaisesti. Alihankinta on sallittu, eikä tarjoajalta edellytetä omaa konekalustoa. Tarjouspyynnöllä annetut arviot perustuvat metsäsuunnitelmaan ja siinä määriteltyyn hakkuiden toteumaan. Arvioissa on huomioitu vuosille 2027-2033 suunnitellut hakkuut: - hakkuukertymä 2000-2500 m3/vuosi - puukaupan tulot 90 000-100 000 euroa/vuosi - hakkuut n. 20 ha/vuosi - metsänhoitotyöt, kuten taimikonhoito, raivaus, istutus tai muut vastaavat työt n. 15-25 ha/vuosi. Vuosittaiset määrät vaihtelevat sen mukaan mitä hakkuita ja töitä kulloinkin toteutetaan. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin, vaan hankinnat tehdään tilaajan tarpeen ja määrärahojen puitteissa. Metsäsuunnitelman ulkopuoliset pienehköt hankintahakkuut (infra-alue, myrskytuho tai muut vastaavat) palveluntuottaja suorittaa puun myynnin parhaaseen mahdolliseen markkinahintaan. Markkinakartoitus ja hankinnan osiin jakaminen: Hankinnan valmisteluvaiheessa on toteutettu markkinakartoitus, joka kuvataan hankinta-asiakirjoissa hankintaa koskevissa lisätiedoissa. Hankintayksikkö kilpailuttaa metsänhoidon palvelusopimuksen yhtenä kokonaisuutena ja valitsee sopimuskaudelle yhden (1) palveluntuottajan. Osiin jakamatta jättämisen perusteena on hankintayksikön oma sekä markkinakartoituksen infotilaisuudessa saatu alan toimijoiden näkemys, että hankinta muodostaa toiminnallisesti luontevan kokonaisuuden, jonka jakaminen osiin ei ole tarkoituksenmukaista. Hankinnan osiin jakaminen lisäisi hallinnollista taakkaa ja koordinointia, nostaisi siten kokonaiskustannuksia logististen ja operatiivisten päällekkäisyyksien vuoksi, sekä hajottaisi vastuita, mikä voisi heikentää metsänhoidon laadun ja aikataulujen hallintaa. Udbuddet gennemføres som et offentligt udbud i henhold til forsyningsvirksomhedsdirektivets art. 45. Rammeaftalen indgås med Aalborg Service A/S som Rammeaftaleholder. Kontraktstyring og administration af Rammeaftalen varetages af Ordregiver. Ordregiver ønsker én Leverandør på Rammeaftalen. Med henvisning til forsyningsvirksomhedsdirektivets artikel 65 har Ordregiver valgt ikke at opdele udbuddet i særskilte delaftaler, idet behovet for korte leveringstider for rør og komponenter samt montage af svejste muffesamlinger med kort varsel bedst imødekommes ved en samlet rammeaftale.

title: Denmark – Relocation services – Rammeaftale om flytteydelser
description: Udbudsprocessen omfatter en aftale med Etablissement- og Terrænkommandoen (ETK) om levering af flytteydelser. ETK udbyder flytteydelser på Forsvarets etablissementer, forstået som flytning imellem etablissementer, på etablissementer, nedtagning samt opbevaring. Flytteydelser kan ligeledes indebære, nedtagning, udpakning og opsætning af kontorpladser fordelt på fem (5) regionale delaftaler. Det nærmere indhold og omfang af ydelserne fremgår af Rammeaftalen. Flytteydelser vil skulle udføres på Forsvarets lokationer som fremgår af Aftalebilag 2 - Etablissement oversigt. Antallet af etablissementer vil kunne ændre sig i aftaleperioden. Udbuddet er opdelt geografisk i følgende fem (5) delaftaler: Delaftale 1: Region Nordjylland Delaftale 2: Region Midtjylland Delaftale 3: Region Syddanmark Delaftale 4: Region Sjælland Delaftale 5: Region Hovedstaden Delaftalerne er opdelt geografisk, for at gøre det muligt for mindre og mellemstore lokale virksomheder at byde på opgaven. Der kan afgives tilbud på en eller flere af de udbudte delaftaler. Tilbudsgiver skal i ESPD del ll.A. angive, hvilke delaftaler I ønsker at afgive tilbud på. Der skal afleveres et (1) tilbud per delaftale, som Tilbudsgiver ønsker at afgive tilbud på. Etablissement- og Terrænkommandoen gør opmærksom på, at det er muligt for en Tilbudsgiver at få tildelt alle delaftaler. Rammeaftalen tildeles to Leverandører, som rangeres på en kaskade på baggrund af ETK's tilbudsevaluering, jf. udbudsbetingelsernes pkt. 4. Konkrete ordrer på Rammeaftalen bliver tildelt som følger: Ordrer tildeles den første Leverandør i kaskaden. Såfremt denne Leverandør ikke kan udføre ordren indenfor den fastsatte frist jf. pkt. 9.1, vil den anden Leverandør i kaskaden blive tildelt ordren. Det estimeres, at Rammeaftalen har en økonomisk værdi på 24 mio. i den samlede kon-traktperiode. Værdien er alene udtryk for ETK’s bedste skøn på udbudstidspunktet, der baserer sig på tidligere indkøb samt kommende forventede indkøb. Skønnet er ikke bindende for ETK eller udtryk for en garanteret minimumsomsætning for Leverandøren. ETK har således ikke pligt til at aftage en bestemt mængde. Rammeaftalens maksimale økonomiske værdi i den samlede kontraktperiode udgør i alt 48 mio. DKK. Det maksimale økonomiske omfang udgør en ret til for ETK at købe via Rammeaftalen uanset indkøbsvolumen måtte overstige den estimerede værdi. Den maksimale økonomiske værdi er et udtryk for en samlet økonomisk værdi for alle delaftalerne og benyttes derfor på tværs af delaftalerne. Rammeaftalen ophører uden varsel, såfremt den maksimale værdi overskrides forud for kontraktperiodens ophør. Årsagen til Rammeaftalens maksimale værdi er risikoen for, at ETK’s fremtidige behov over-stiger det på udbudstidspunktet estimerede behov særligt henset til den øgede økonomi og aktivitetsniveau i Forsvaret som følge af Forsvarsforliget for 2024-2033, Aftale om styrkelse af Forsvarets kampkraft af 22. februar 2025 og den nuværende sikkerhedspolitiske situation.

description: U.S. Department of Commerce | NOAA | Acquisition and Grants Office REQUEST FOR INFORMATION U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis Issue date: November 18, 2026 Responses due: December 2, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. EST / 5:00 p.m. MST Questions requested by: November 24, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. EST / noon MST Responses and questions: Email both contacts below. Kyle Shaffer, Contracting Officer | kyle.shaffer@noaa.gov Nicholas Brown, Contract Specialist | nicholas.g.brown@noaa.gov Issuing office: NOAA Acquisition and Grants Office, Western Acquisition Division - Boulder 1. Purpose and acquisition status NOAA seeks information from firms capable of performing seafood supply-chain mapping, risk analysis, and complex data analysis for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of International Affairs, Trade, and Commerce (IATC). Responses will help NOAA refine the requirement, assess available expertise, identify data and access needs, inform budget planning and the independent Government cost estimate (IGCE), and determine an acquisition approach. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation. NOAA does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI and will not pay for the information requested or response preparation. Responses are information only, not quotations or offers. NOAA may or may not issue a solicitation. A response is not required to participate in a future competition. Responses are welcome from all interested sources, including small and other-than-small businesses. The acquisition vehicle and set-aside for a future procurement have not been determined. NAICS 541690 is the preliminary classification. Respondents may recommend another code with an explanation. 2. Background and objectives IATC administers the Seafood Import Monitoring Program (SIMP) and supports trade policy initiatives concerning U.S. seafood exports. SIMP uses harvest, landing, and chain-of-custody information to help detect and deter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and misrepresentation in seafood entering the U.S. market. NOAA seeks analytical support to: Map supply chains. Further develop existing mapping and identify custodians at each node from harvest through U.S. import, including U.S. territories. Prioritize and analyze risk. Identify priority supply chains and examine species covered by SIMP and other species of NMFS interest for IUU-fishing and misrepresentation risks. Analyze U.S. re-imports. Examine processing and market dynamics for U.S.-sourced seafood and imports that directly compete with key U.S. seafood products. 3. Data, equipment, and onboarding assumptions Use the following assumptions when describing capability, schedule, and resource needs. They describe NOAA's current planning, not final contract terms or authorization to access data. Identify any assumption that would prevent performance or materially affect the proposed approach. Period of performance. NOAA is planning completion of all four milestones within 12 months of the contract or task-order effective date, including onboarding, analysis, and Government review. Respondents should address the feasibility of this schedule and opportunities for earlier completion. Data and systems. The planned environment includes NOAA Fisheries instances of BigQuery and Looker, and Government Google Workspace tools such as Sheets, Docs, and Drive. NOAA anticipates providing aggregated key-data-element tables, relevant importer documents used in SIMP audits, existing work products, data architecture guides, and field definitions. Public sources include Census trade data and the NOAA Fisheries foreign trade portal. Individual access would depend on need-to-know, required nondisclosure agreements, and security approval. Equipment and approved tools. For planning, assume project work, data, and deliverables remain on NOAA-furnished laptops and approved Government systems, not contractor-owned devices. The initial equipment planning basis is five laptops, not a staffing minimum or maximum. Additional equipment needs may be identified but are not guaranteed. R and R Shiny are contemplated tools, with installation by the NOAA Fisheries Help Desk. Do not assume permission to install unapproved software or use a new service. Recommended alternatives may be identified for Government consideration. Data protection and transmission. Plan to exchange protected project information through Kiteworks or another NOAA-approved secure method, not ordinary email alone. Explain how employees, subcontractors, and subject-matter experts would work within the same access and information-handling restrictions. Artificial intelligence tools. Trade-confidential data from BigQuery or Looker must not be used in AI tools. Public-data use in NOAA Fisheries' Gemini environment may be considered subject to Government approval. Do not assume approval for other AI tools. Identify any proposed use and the data involved. Onboarding and continuity. For schedule comparison, use a planning allowance of 60 to 90 calendar days for Public Trust processing, followed by approximately one to two weeks for account provisioning and equipment readiness after security approval when equipment is available. These are response-planning assumptions, not guaranteed processing times. Additional equipment or replacement personnel may require more time. Identify the schedule effect of delays and the work that could proceed without protected data or system access. The public NMFS Partner Government Agency (PGA) Message Set Guidelines describe reporting fields and data relationships; they do not make the underlying import or audit records public. No access to non-public data or analysis of actual NOAA records is requested in response to this RFI. NMFS PGA Message Set Guidelines https://www.cbp.gov/document/guidance/nmfs-pga-message-set-guidelines 4. Proposed milestones and billing approach NOAA is considering firm-fixed-price services with payments tied to Government acceptance of the following milestone outputs. The milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment terms are not final. Respondents should identify practical improvements. I. Initial mapping and data development Onboard, review existing work, and complete or refine initial supply-chain mapping, including source fisheries, landing locations, and primary processing entities. Provide a data table suitable for BigQuery and an electronic summary of the work completed and initial supply chains identified for further analysis. II. Prioritized supply chains Develop the list of priority supply chains for further analysis, building on the Government-provided mapping. Provide the prioritization document and supporting documentation, including the source-fishery, landing, and primary-processing information used. III. Near-final mapping and analysis Provide updated supply-chain mapping, analysis of priority supply chains, and re-import analysis. Include an updated BigQuery data table, supporting analytical materials, and research and summaries of source-fishery regulations and laws, including harvesting nations' legal species and harvesting methods relevant to U.S. imports. IV. Final reports and data Complete internal and public reports with visuals, supporting documentation, and the final BigQuery data table containing supply-chain mapping and additional analysis. Reports and supporting documents are contemplated as electronic deliverables. Any hard-copy requirement would be specified in a solicitation. 5. description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District will be issuing Invitation for Bids for the Wareham Harbor Federal Navigation Project, located in Wareham, Massachusetts. This procurement is a Small Business Set Aside Invitation for Bid (IFB). The NAICS code for the work is 237990 with a size standard of $37M. Construction is expected to take about five months to complete. The estimated construction cost is $1,000,000 to $5,000,000. Any responsible source meeting this standard may submit a bid to be considered by the New England District. The Wareham Harbor FNP consists of a 2.4 mile long, 9-foot deep Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) channel. The channel is comprised of several reaches of varying widths (100-ft to 250-ft widths) to include the entrance channel through Cromeset Neck Reach, Quahaug Bar Reach, Parkwood Beach Reach, and the Inner Harbor Reach. Transit from Wareham to CCBDS will occur through the Cape Cod Canal. A smaller portion of the material is sand (approx. 1,000 CY) and will be placed beneficially at a nearshore site off of Church's Beach in Cuttyhunk, Massachusetts (approximately 28 miles away). title: U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / SOURCES SOUGHT U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis Issue date: November 18, 2026 Responses due: December 02, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Mountain Standard Time (MST) Questions requested by: November 24, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. MST Responses and questions: Email both contacts below. Kyle Shaffer, Contracting Officer | kyle.shaffer@noaa.gov Nicholas Brown, Contract Specialist | nicholas.g.brown@noaa.gov Issuing office: NOAA Acquisition and Grants Office, Western Acquisition Division - Boulder Purpose and acquisition status NOAA seeks information from firms capable of performing seafood supply-chain mapping, risk analysis, and complex data analysis for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of International Affairs, Trade, and Commerce (IATC). Responses will help NOAA refine the requirement, assess available expertise, identify data and access needs, inform budget planning and the independent Government cost estimate (IGCE), and determine an acquisition approach. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation. NOAA does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI and will not pay for the information requested or response preparation. Responses are information only, not quotations or offers. NOAA may or may not issue a solicitation. A response is not required to participate in a future competition. Responses are welcome from small and other-than-small businesses and other interested organizations. Participation is not limited to holders of GSA or NOAA ProTech contracts. NOAA has not selected an acquisition vehicle or made a set-aside determination. NAICS 541715 is the preliminary classification; 541990 is an alternative under consideration. Respondents may recommend another code with an explanation. Background and objectives IATC administers the Seafood Import Monitoring Program (SIMP) and supports trade policy initiatives concerning U.S. seafood exports. SIMP uses harvest, landing, and chain-of-custody information to help detect and deter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and misrepresentation in seafood entering the U.S. market. NOAA seeks analytical support to: Map supply chains. Further develop existing mapping and identify custodians at each node from harvest through U.S. import, including U.S. territories. Prioritize and analyze risk. Identify priority supply chains and examine species covered by SIMP and other species of NMFS interest for IUU-fishing and misrepresentation risks. Analyze U.S. re-imports. Examine processing and market dynamics for U.S.-sourced seafood and imports that directly compete with key U.S. seafood products. Data, equipment, and onboarding assumptions Use the following assumptions when describing capability, schedule, and resource needs. They describe NOAA's current planning, not final contract terms or authorization to access data. Identify any assumption that would prevent performance or materially affect the proposed approach. Period of performance. NOAA is planning completion of all four milestones within 12 months of the contract or task-order effective date, including onboarding, analysis, and Government review. Respondents should address the feasibility of this schedule and opportunities for earlier completion. Data and systems. The planned environment includes NOAA Fisheries instances of BigQuery and Looker, and Government Google Workspace tools such as Sheets, Docs, and Drive. NOAA anticipates providing aggregated key-data-element tables, relevant importer documents used in SIMP audits, existing work products, data architecture guides, and field definitions. Public sources include Census trade data and the NOAA Fisheries foreign trade portal. Individual access would depend on need-to-know, required nondisclosure agreements, and security approval. Equipment and approved tools. For planning, assume project work, data, and deliverables remain on NOAA-furnished laptops and approved Government systems, not contractor-owned devices. The initial equipment planning basis is five laptops, not a staffing minimum or maximum. Additional equipment needs may be identified but are not guaranteed. R and R Shiny are contemplated tools, with installation by the NOAA Fisheries Help Desk. Do not assume permission to install unapproved software or use a new service. Recommended alternatives may be identified for Government consideration. Data protection and transmission. Plan to exchange protected project information through Kiteworks or another NOAA-approved secure method, not ordinary email alone. Explain how employees, subcontractors, and subject-matter experts would work within the same access and information-handling restrictions. Artificial intelligence tools. Trade-confidential data from BigQuery or Looker must not be used in AI tools. Public-data use in NOAA Fisheries' Gemini environment may be considered subject to Government approval. Do not assume approval for other AI tools. Identify any proposed use and the data involved. Onboarding and continuity. For schedule comparison, use a planning allowance of 60 to 90 calendar days for Public Trust processing, followed by approximately one to two weeks for account provisioning and equipment readiness after security approval when equipment is available. These are response-planning assumptions, not guaranteed processing times. Additional equipment or replacement personnel may require more time. Identify the schedule effect of delays and the work that could proceed without protected data or system access. The public NMFS Partner Government Agency (PGA) Message Set Guidelines describe reporting fields and data relationships; they do not make the underlying import or audit records public. No access to non-public data or analysis of actual NOAA records is requested in response to this RFI. NMFS PGA Message Set Guidelines https://www.cbp.gov/document/guidance/nmfs-pga-message-set-guidelines Proposed milestones and billing approach NOAA is considering firm-fixed-price services with payments tied to Government acceptance of the following milestone outputs. The milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment terms are not final. Respondents should identify practical improvements. Milestone | Draft outputs I. Initial mapping and data development | Onboard, review existing work, and complete or refine initial supply-chain mapping, including source fisheries, landing locations, and primary processing entities. Provide a data table suitable for BigQuery and an electronic summary of the work completed and initial supply chains identified for further analysis. II. Prioritized supply chains | Develop the list of priority supply chains for further analysis, building on the Government-provided mapping. Provide the prioritization document and supporting documentation, including the source-fishery, landing, and primary-processing information used. III. Near-final mapping and analysis | Provide updated supply-chain mapping, analysis of priority supply chains, and re-import analysis. Include an updated BigQuery data table, supporting analytical materials, and research and summaries of source-fishery regulations and laws, including harvesting nations' legal species and harvesting methods relevant to U.S. imports. IV. Final reports and data | Complete internal and public reports with visuals, supporting documentation, and the final BigQuery data table containing supply-chain mapping and additional analysis. Reports and supporting documents are contemplated as electronic deliverables. Any hard-copy requirement would be specified in a solicitation. Information requested Provide a company information sheet and a narrative addressing the numbered questions on the following pages. Use the question numbers and state the assumptions behind each response. Brief, specific answers are preferred to general marketing materials. No completed analysis, detailed technical proposal, or binding price quotation is requeste
